title: Trim Video – Cut the Start and End Online, No Upload
description: Cut the start or end off a video: play it, mark the start and end, and save just that part. Works in your browser with nothing uploaded.
heading: Trim a Video
subtitle: Keep only the part of a video you want by marking where it starts and ends; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Remove the shaky start of a recording or the long wait at the end. Play the video, pause where the part you want begins and click Set start here, then do the same for the end. You can also type the times, like 0:12.5. The page shows how long the new video will be before you save it.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your video is cut by your own browser and never sent to a server.

features.title: Mark while you watch
features.text: Set the start and end from the player's current position, or type exact times.

features.title: Same format
features.text: MP4 stays MP4 and WebM stays WebM, ready to share.

steps.title: Choose a video
steps.text: Pick a video or drop it on the page.

steps.title: Mark the part to keep
steps.text: Play the video and click Set start here and Set end here, or type the times.

steps.title: Trim and download
steps.text: Click Trim video, check the result and download it.

handles: Start and end: set from the player or typed as minutes and seconds, to a tenth of a second.
Sound: kept, cut at the same points as the picture. If your browser can't read it, the page tells you the result has no sound.
Formats: MP4, WebM, MOV and MKV keep their format; M4V and 3GP videos become MP4.
limits: Only the first chosen video is trimmed.
One part is kept per run; to remove a part in the middle, trim twice and join the parts with Merge videos.
A WebM or MKV whose start you change is encoded again, so a long one takes longer.

faq.question: Is my video uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Trimming is done by your own browser, on your device, with the video encoders built into it. Nothing is sent to a server; open your browser's network panel while it runs and you will see no upload.

faq.question: How do I cut out the middle of a video?
faq.answer: Trim the video twice, once for the part before and once for the part after, then put the two parts together with Merge videos.

faq.question: How exact is the cut?
faq.answer: You can set times to a tenth of a second. The new video starts and ends at those times.

faq.question: Does trimming lower the quality?
faq.answer: Not for an MP4 or MOV: its picture, H.264, HEVC from recent iPhones, VP9 or AV1, is copied as it is, not encoded again. An MKV or a WebM is copied too when you only cut its end. Otherwise the kept part is encoded again at a high quality, so it looks very close to the original.

faq.question: Which browsers does it work in?
faq.answer: Recent Chrome and Edge read and make the most formats; Safari and Firefox work with most videos. If your browser can't read or make a codec, the page names it and says what to try instead.

faq.question: Will the trimmed video play on my phone and in WhatsApp?
faq.answer: An MP4 or MOV keeps its format, which phones and chat apps open, and other videos such as M4V become MP4. A WebM or MKV stays WebM or MKV, which some phones and apps refuse: convert it afterwards with Video converter. To make it smaller as well, use Compress video next.
